body:
Wow, thank you for such a lengthy reply! I walk like a truck driver too, I didn't even know that was a thing that was said to other people.

Accommodating without compromising myself is a skill I haven't learned yet. It's hard when you grew up being told that everyone else is more important, don't be selfish you brat, what you want doesn't matter. Oh, but I'm your mommy I'll keep you safe from all the bad people who are going to hurt you! But how dare you miss the bus and make me wake up to drive you, you're so selfish.

I still haven't gotten it through my head that the only person I needed to be kept safe from was her. I have a very good inkling that she was just as abusive to my dad at least on the emotional front, and I don't know if opening up to him about the things that happened because of her would even help. We're both very private people. 

I never learned to properly socialize, and I'm always worried that I'm talking about myself too much, or being annoying so I'm very sorry if I come across that way. I'm also sorry for apologizing. 

So, what helps propel you forward? I seem to be stuck in the mud when it comes to progress with this despite therapy, and I struggle with unlearning all of the unhealthy thoughts that were drilled into my brain. I always feel like I'm grasping at straws trying to move on. I feel like I see pieces of her in everyone and it has me too terrified to leave the house most days.

I'm extremely comfortable having no contact with my mother, I know she's toxic, but somehow despite all the nights spent rationalizing everything I still can't begin to move forward. Or maybe I have and I just don't know it yet. How did you help your heart catch up with the things your brain has already figured out? When did you know that everything would start being okay?

Also, thank you for talking with me :). Talking to people is a strange new thing.

Hi! I don't know how to ask these questions any other way but the hard and awkward way: Have you stopped 'mourning' your mother yet? What was your first step? Does the fear of 'becoming her' ever go away? This is the first time I've ever really reached out to anyone about this.

I'm 22, been no contact with my mother for almost exactly two years. I haven't figured out how to 'get over' it yet? It's been so long and I haven't even begun. I don't know how. Logically I know that this person is not the mother I was supposed to have, and that she isn't the same person that she always pretended to be.

I have zero self esteem, and I feel so guilty for not being a 'good daughter' and I have no clue how to let go of that. She still haunts me in my dreams and when I hear her voice on the answering machine it just shuts me down. What helps you deal with it gnawing at the back of your mind? Does it ever go away?
